solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Decide to deal with later, after page one

parts.note: post- means after, as in post-war
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shelves a decision until they have read the first page.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off a matter, deciding to tackle it at some later time, is to delay it.

clue.text: Spiel Father Time interrupts

indicators.note: the time piece breaks into the father word

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: Father Time breaks in on someone's sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Patter is glib rapid talk, such as a salesman's spiel.

clue.text: Doctor hates hospital case

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor who hates a particular hospital case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a patient, but it is the definition: a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting case or cover, as for a blade.

clue.text: Good enough, as port proved to be after dinner

definitions.text: as port proved to be after dinner
definitions.meaning: at the end of a formal dinner the port is handed round the table, so it could be handed on

explanation.definitionFit: The word means adequate, and literally capable of being handed along, like the port decanter.

clue.text: How Carmen is shown to be heartless, as usual

parts.note: split as heart-less: less means none, and the heart is what is missing

indicators.note: with heartless, says what Carmen is shown without: its central pair of letters

explanation.surface: Carmen, as so often, is played as a heartless woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'heartless' as heart + less: Carmen's heart, its central pair, with 'no' in front for the 'less'.
explanation.definitionFit: What is standard or customary is the done thing, the usual pattern.

clue.text: Among vast number retracted, offer stands

indicators.note: the offer is placed among the letters of the other piece
drawn back, so the word for a vast number is read backwards

parts.note: a sea of faces is a vast number of them
a bid is an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A bid made amid a crowd that has pulled back still stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vast number' is a sea, as in a sea of faces; 'retracted' turns it round before 'Among' takes in the offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abides and stands are synonyms in the sense of tolerates or puts up with, as in can't stand it.

clue.text: Prepare something to eat, breaking up blackjack

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to jack a car up is to raise it

explanation.surface: Someone makes a snack while breaking off a game of blackjack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' tells you to split blackjack into black and jack; 'up' also belongs with jack.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a covered pot, a way of preparing food.

clue.text: Put off and fed up, went wrong

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone was put off and fed up because things went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' reads as one idiom, but in a down clue 'up' turns the word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferred means postponed, put off until later.

clue.text: Ram home

parts.note: looks like a verb, to force a point; read as noun phrase it is a place where a male sheep lives

explanation.surface: Force something firmly into place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is a fenced enclosure for a flock, so a ram's lodging.

clue.text: 'Pearl Beyond Price' — tear-jerking, doubtless

indicators.note: the letters of the word tear are jerked about into a new order

parts.note: sure means certain, beyond doubt

explanation.surface: Reads like a review of a weepy film called 'Pearl Beyond Price'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear-jerking' splits: 'jerking' is the anagram signal for tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl beyond price is a priceless thing, a precious possession or hoard of great value.

clue.text: Very loud — pack round to mute sound

indicators.note: the pack goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a bale is a bundle or pack of goods
ff (fortissimo) is the musical notation for very loud

explanation.surface: Something is very loud, so pack material around it to deaden the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To damp or muffle noise is a verb sense, as with a baffle board in a loudspeaker.

clue.text: Short of time, set aside criminal complaint

indicators.note: something criminal is bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A case is set aside for lack of time in a criminal complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of time' means losing a T: SET ASIDE without T is rearranged ('criminal').
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or ailment, as in a chest complaint.

clue.text: Yesterday's star performing as uncredited cast

parts.note: ex- means former, so yesterday's man is an ex

indicators.note: the letters of star are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A faded former star now appears only among the unnamed cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' is the anagram signal; 'as' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Film extras are the background performers who get no screen credit.

clue.text: Express excursion skirting southern runway

indicators.note: the two pieces sit either side of the letter for southern, running round its edges

parts.note: to air a view is to express it
a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: An express coach trip goes round the south to reach an airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of ground where light aircraft take off and land serves as a runway.

clue.text: Says it with music?

parts.note: chanting in a singsong voice is saying with music; split as two words it also means within musical notes

explanation.surface: Echoes the phrase 'say it with flowers'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to chant or recite in a level, singsong voice.

clue.text: With key, opens up and takes a look

parts.note: G is a musical key
to lance a boil is to cut it open

explanation.surface: Someone with a key unlocks a door and peers inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Glances are quick looks, so to do so is to take a brief look.

clue.text: Dog with best time, according to announcement

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: the peak of a career is its best time

explanation.surface: A dog wins with the best time, so the announcer declares.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese, the small flat-faced Chinese breed, is a toy dog.

clue.text: Sharp decline in confectionery

parts.note: acid means sharp or sour in taste
a drop is a fall or decline

explanation.surface: A steep fall in sweet sales.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid drop is a tart boiled sweet, a British confection.

clue.text: Put up the ladder and urge me to fake breaking in

indicators.note: the jumbled letters break into the urge word

parts.note: to prod someone is to urge them on

indicators.note: something fake is not genuine, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone urged to fake a break-in is told to put up a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' turns ME TO into MOTE, and 'breaking in' puts it into PROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised in rank is moving up the career ladder.

clue.text: Support also waveringly given to suggestion

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: unsteadily, so the letters of also are wobbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion is half-heartedly backed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waveringly' is the anagram signal; 'given to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a suggestion put forward for consideration.

clue.text: Middle, beginning or end of course

indicators.note: the beginning of the word course is its first letter
the end of the word course is its last letter

explanation.surface: Looks like a question about where to stand on a race course.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'beginning or end of course' literally: C, then OR, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its central part, its heart or middle.

clue.text: Partner does nothing right

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, to con them
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A lazy partner is accused of never doing anything right.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or companion, especially of a monarch.

clue.text: Admission to course

definitions.meaning: a dish served at a meal, the main one in the US or the one before it in Britain

explanation.surface: Reads as being let in to a college or golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means entry, and also a dish served at a meal.

clue.text: Show how much you love jalopy referred to as 'she'?

parts.note: a jalopy is an old car
-ess is the suffix marking a female, as in lioness

explanation.surface: Fond owners call their old banger 'she' and show it love.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle loving stroke, a way to show affection.

clue.text: Accustomed, coming from college, to turn left?

indicators.note: turning the college word round reads it backwards

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
red means left-wing politically

explanation.surface: Students arrive at college and turn left-wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses the college word; red is the colour of the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: Inured means hardened or habituated to something unpleasant.

clue.text: Mad about me — warped

indicators.note: the warped word goes around the other piece

parts.note: something dented is bent out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone is crazy about the speaker in a twisted way.
explanation.definitionFit: Demented means out of one's mind, crazy.

clue.text: He parted from her in foreign country: a wrench

indicators.note: the remaining letter goes in the name of the country

parts.note: Spain is a country abroad from a British viewpoint

indicators.note: he is separated from her, leaving one letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple splitting up abroad: a painful wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He parted from her' is literal: remove those two letters from her, leaving one letter for 'in' to place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a twisting injury to a joint, as is a wrench.

clue.text: Arrive to take care of number one

parts.note: c/o, CO, is the abbreviation for care of
number one means oneself, me

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to look after themselves first.
explanation.definitionFit: To come is to arrive, reach a place.

clue.text: Answer HMRC demand?

definitions.meaning: to answer back is to reply or retort
HMRC, the UK tax authority, demands a tax form from each taxpayer

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to respond to a tax bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To return is to reply; a tax return is the form HMRC requires each year.

clue.text: During much worse novel, give up

indicators.note: the shuffled letters fall inside the other word

parts.note: far, as in far too much, means much

indicators.note: new, so the letters of worse are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A reader abandons a novel that has got much worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' is far, as in far worse; 'novel' is the anagram signal and 'During' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or abjure something on oath is to give it up.

clue.text: Walked past home having dined, dropped in

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's home or flat

indicators.note: the word in is dropped out of the other word

explanation.surface: Someone strolled past their place after eating out and called in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes IN from DINED to leave DED.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad is to walk softly or steadily, so padded is walked.

clue.text: Saw one's been taken in by crooked dealer

indicators.note: the piece for one's goes inside the jumbled word
bent out of shape, so the letters of dealer are rearranged

parts.note: I is one, and one's is I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone realises they have been conned by a dishonest dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is one as a numeral letter plus S; 'crooked' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to see it, in the sense of grasping or understanding it.
